question.text: Two slits, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math>, illuminated by a white light source, give a white central maximum. A transparent sheet, of refractive index <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>25</mn></math> and thickness <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math>, is placed in front of <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math>. Another transparent sheet, of refractive index <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>50</mn></math> and thickness <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>, is placed in front of <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math>. If the central maxima are not affected, then the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>:</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> will be

solution.text:
Since there is no shift in central maxima, the path difference introduced by the two sheets are equal.

i.e. μ1-1t1=μ2-1t2

Where μ1 and μ2 are refraction index

i.e. t1t2=(μ2-1)(μ1-1)=(1.5-1)(1.25-1)=0.50.25=2
